clue.text: Quite low voice exhibited by good number

parts.note: the alto is the lowest female singing voice
a number is something that numbs, and ether was the classic anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A singer's low part is put on show by a fine piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is read as 'numb-er', a thing that deadens feeling, a long-standing crossword trick; 'exhibited by' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether can mean entirely or completely, the same as quite in 'quite finished'.

clue.text: President wrong over new institution of the law

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was a US president
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A president does wrong over a new law body.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln's Inn is one of London's four Inns of Court where barristers belong; 'over' places the pieces in order down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln's Inn is one of the Inns of Court, a professional institution for barristers.

clue.text: Completed shed for people moving out of slums?

parts.note: over means finished or completed
to shed blood is to spill it

explanation.surface: A finished hut becomes housing for relocated slum dwellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a hut but is a verb, spill.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is surplus population rehoused from crowded city areas into new towns.

clue.text: Country life finally more impecunious, some say

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word before it
some say means a word is pronounced aloud and its sound is entered

parts.note: stonier means more stony-broke, poorer

explanation.surface: In a country, life is ending even poorer, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: Stony broke is British slang for penniless; said in a non-rhotic accent, stonier sounds like STONIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country in northern Europe.

clue.text: All gathered for this service?

parts.note: echoes the hymn line 'All is safely gathered in', sung at a church thanksgiving when crops are in

explanation.definitionFit: This church thanksgiving service celebrates the crops all being gathered in.

clue.text: One copying material, needing to decorate

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
an aper is one who apes, or copies

explanation.surface: A copyist needs fabric to do up a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaper is to put up fresh wallpaper, a way to redecorate a room.

clue.text: Apostle said to become tedious here

indicators.note: said signals that the word for the apostle is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: Paul is the apostle who wrote many New Testament epistles

explanation.surface: A saint reputedly found this spot boring.
explanation.walkthrough: PAUL and PALL sound the same; 'here' simply points the solver to the grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To pall is to lose interest or grow wearisome, the verb sense of tiresome repetition.

clue.text: Old Spanish kingdom lacking a noble element

indicators.note: lacking means the following letter is taken out of the kingdom's name

parts.note: Aragon was a medieval kingdom in north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A historic Spanish realm without a single aristocratic member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noble' suggests aristocrats but means a noble gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is one of the noble gases, the unreactive chemical elements.

clue.text: We forget having eaten this large amount, you and me

parts.note: a lot is a large amount
us means you and me

explanation.surface: We forget a great deal after a big meal shared between us.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey, the lotus-eaters forget home after eating the lotus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend eating the lotus made people forget everything, so it is the food of forgetfulness.

clue.text: He discovers gold in passage at the front

indicators.note: at the front puts the earlier pieces before the word for gold

parts.note: a vent is a passage or opening for air or smoke
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A prospector finds gold in a tunnel near the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold looks like the thing the man discovers, but it is only wordplay; 'at the front' puts the first two pieces ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventor comes up with or devises something new, which is a kind of discovering.

clue.text: Promise jam

definitions.meaning: to ... is to pledge, as in ... one's troth
a jam is a tight spot or predicament

explanation.definitionFit: Plight means both to pledge one's word and a difficult situation one is stuck in.

clue.text: Meat for someone else? Nothing eaten by good boy

indicators.note: eaten by means the zero goes inside the other letters, swallowed up

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good
nothing is zero, the letter O
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A good lad refuses his dinner, which another would gladly eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'one man's meat is another man's poison'.
explanation.definitionFit: From the proverb, what nourishes one person is harmful to another, so another's meat is this.

clue.text: Sets out east with a tenner?

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a tenner is ten pounds, X being the Roman ten

explanation.surface: Someone heads east carrying a ten-pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note; read as X POUNDS it supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound something is to set it out or explain it in detail.

clue.text: Dress style of the French army housed in school

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: housed in means the army letters sit inside the school

parts.note: a college is a school
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A French fashion for soldiers stationed at an academy.
explanation.walkthrough: COLLEGE opens as COLLE+TA+GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Décolletage is a low neckline on a dress, a style of cut.

clue.text: One against keeping theatre company in capital

indicators.note: keeping means the outer word holds the company inside it

parts.note: A1, read as letters AI, means first-rate, as does capital as an exclamation
NT is the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: An opponent is holding a drama troupe in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city but means excellent, A1; the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is anti is opposed to something, a person against it.

clue.text: Tremor naturally disrupting for a sketch

indicators.note: disrupting signals the letters of the following words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A tremor spoils someone's attempt at drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of FOR A SKETCH are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftershock is a smaller tremor following the main quake of an earthquake.

clue.text: Ideologue's bad luck finally changed

indicators.note: finally changed means the closing letter of the phrase is swapped for another

parts.note: hard lines is a British expression for bad luck

explanation.surface: A zealot's misfortune turns around at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard lines!' is British for 'tough luck!'; the final S becomes R. 'Ideologue's' is 'ideologue is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner sticks rigidly to a doctrine, as an ideologue does.

clue.text: Current power source filling economist's vehicle with energy

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a famous economist, so Mill's gives these letters

indicators.note: filling, with 'with', means the energy letter is placed inside the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An economist's car is stuffed with energy to make power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' but is a flow of water; the def is the whole phrase 'Current power source'.
explanation.definitionFit: A millstream is the flowing water that drives a mill wheel, a current supplying power.

clue.text: Smuggling vehicles

definitions.meaning: illicit trading, as in drug dealing
the cars and lorries on a road

explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means both illegal trade in goods and the vehicles moving along roads.

clue.text: Rodent's breeding frenzy holding up Noah's work

indicators.note: holding means the outer word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: must or musth is the frenzied state of male elephants in the breeding season

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Noah built the ark

explanation.surface: A rodent's mating frenzy delays Noah's building of the ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal and 'up' turns Noah's vessel upwards, as a down clue is read; musth is the rut of bull elephants.
explanation.definitionFit: The muskrat is a large aquatic rodent of North America.

clue.text: Burn badly on back of boiler

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A scald on the rear of a heating boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: Burn is the Scottish word for a stream, not an injury; 'on' places the letter before ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A burn and a rill are both small streams of running water.

clue.text: Classy dancer wasted time and put little into role

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: wasted means the letters of the word for performer are wrecked and remade

explanation.surface: A posh dancer wasted time and gave a weak performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' signals the anagram of the performer word, which sits between the class letter and the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To underact is to perform a part with too little energy or expression.

clue.text: It's taboo to drop an older relative

indicators.note: to drop means the two letters are let fall from the word for forbidden

parts.note: unclean means ritually forbidden, taboo

explanation.surface: It is forbidden to abandon an elderly family member.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a relative from an older generation, a parent's brother.

clue.text: Foreign wife

definitions.meaning: an old sense of foreign, especially German or Low Countries
in Cockney, 'my old ...' means my wife

explanation.definitionFit: Dutch once broadly meant foreign or German, and 'old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife.

clue.text: Using ointment, runs for some silverware

parts.note: to salve is to apply ointment
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone smears ointment and scores runs for a silver trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A salver is a flat tray, often silver, used for serving.

clue.text: Deadline for disconnection?

definitions.meaning: a final limit, the point beyond which nothing is accepted
a stopping of supply, as when electricity is cut

explanation.definitionFit: A cut-off is both a final time limit and an interruption of supply, such as the power being shut off.

clue.text: Have problems accepting foreign money in gallery

indicators.note: accepting means the scrambled word takes the currency inside it
having problems signals the letters of 'Have' are disordered

parts.note: the rand is the South African currency

explanation.surface: Someone has difficulty taking foreign cash in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problems' turns HAVE into VEAH, which 'accepting' opens to hold RAND: VE+RAND+AH.
explanation.definitionFit: A verandah is a roofed gallery or porch along the outside of a house.

clue.text: Typical opening lines once cut by German playwright

indicators.note: cut means the starting letters are removed from the playwright's name

parts.note: Bertolt Brecht was a German dramatist
BR, British Rail, is the former railway lines, here at the start of the name

explanation.surface: A typical first scene was trimmed by a German dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening lines' suggests a play's first words; it means the BR at the front of BRECHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is German for genuine or authentic, the true typical article.

clue.text: Cure taken in the days after Christmas?

definitions.meaning: an abrupt complete withdrawal from an addictive drug as treatment

definitions.text: taken in the days after Christmas?
definitions.meaning: leftover festive bird, served chilled and eaten after the Christmas meal

explanation.definitionFit: Cold turkey is both sudden withdrawal treatment for addiction and literally the chilled leftover Christmas roast.
